title: glosa theory-evidence-falsifier matrix row
description: tier: Dr (specified; independently unreviewed). One row per theoretical proposition of a theory-building or conceptual paper, narrated by methodology/P26_claim_evidence_theory_matrix.md item (f) (founder instruction 2026-09-25). Chain per row: claim -> logical basis (mechanism in the author's own words, then its premises, each premise cited through claim_evidence_matrix rows) -> supporting literature -> contradictory literature -> boundary conditions -> observable implication -> falsifier. One-fact-one-home: the proposition's canonical text and its falsifier live on the claim card (claim_ref -> claim_card.claim_id; claim_card.five_questions.tested.falsifier), never restated here; literature is referenced through claim_evidence_matrix_row ids (cem-...), never re-described here. What this row is the only home of: the mechanism statement, its premises, boundary conditions, the observable implication, and rival explanations. Namespace https://glosa.example/ is a placeholder.

proposition_id.description: The proposition's label inside the manuscript (P1, P2, P2a, ...).

claim_ref.description: Pointer to claim_card.claim_id: the proposition IS a claim card. Its canonical wording (statement.text) and its falsifier (five_questions.tested.falsifier) live there.

claim_label.description: Optional short display handle; the claim card wins on any disagreement.

constructs.description: Construct names this proposition relates (same vocabulary as claim_evidence_matrix_row.construct).

logical_basis.description: The 'no argument by citation' rule (P26 item h), made structural: the mechanism is stated in the author's own words FIRST; citations attach only to its parts (premises), never stand in for the mechanism itself.

mechanism.description: Why the proposition should hold, in the author's own words. A sentence that is only a citation ('as X showed') is not a mechanism.

cem_refs.description: claim_evidence_matrix_row ids backing this premise. Empty = the premise is the author's own reasoning step or a definition (legal; say so in `kind`).

contradictory_literature.description: cem row ids carrying evidence or argument against the proposition. May be empty only with contradictory_search_ref (NC-27: LOCAL_EVIDENCE_NOT_FOUND != NO_LOCAL_EVIDENCE_EXISTS, generalised: not found != does not exist).

boundary_conditions.description: Conditions under which the proposition is NOT expected to hold (non-occurrence conditions, scope limits). At least one.

observable_implication.description: What should be observable, and by what readout, if the proposition holds.

falsifier_on_card.description: true iff the checker confirmed that claim_card(claim_ref).five_questions.tested.falsifier states an observation at this proposition's grain (not a TODO placeholder, not a strength-of-claim sentence -- kernel rule29). The falsifier text itself is never copied into this row.

rival_explanations.description: Rival theories or mechanisms that would produce the same observable implication, each with the observation that would tell them apart. May be empty only with rival_search_ref.

allOf.description: Empty contradictory_literature requires a named challenge search.
Empty rival_explanations requires a named search for rivals.
A row may not advance past Draft while its falsifier is unconfirmed on the claim card.
